steps.title: Check if other devices have internet
steps.detail: Try a phone on the same Wi-Fi and another computer. If nothing has internet, the problem is the connection, not this computer.
steps.why: It tells you whether to fix this computer or call your provider.

steps.title: Check that Wi-Fi is on and airplane mode is off
steps.detail: Click the network icon at the bottom right of the screen. Make sure Wi-Fi is on and airplane mode is off, then pick your network.
steps.why: A switch turned off by mistake is the most common cause.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

steps.title: Restart the modem and router
steps.detail: Unplug the internet box (modem and router) from power, wait 30 seconds, plug it back in and wait until its lights are steady.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows
steps.do_not: Do not press the reset button on the box: it can erase its settings.

steps.title: Run the network troubleshooter
steps.detail: In Windows, open Settings, then the network troubleshooter, and follow what it says.
steps.why: Windows can find and fix common network problems by itself.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

steps.title: Forget the Wi-Fi network and join again
steps.detail: In the Wi-Fi settings, choose your network, select Forget, then connect again with the Wi-Fi password.
steps.why: A saved connection can go wrong after a password or box change.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

steps.title: If nothing has internet, call your provider
steps.detail: Call from a mobile phone. Ask if there is an outage in your area and write down the ticket number.
steps.why: Outages on the provider's side can only be fixed by them.

steps.title: Still stuck? Call your IT contact
steps.detail: Tell them what you tried and what you see on screen. A photo of the screen helps.
steps.why: They can check settings and equipment you cannot reach.
